answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register identities by locking cryptographic stake into a burn contract. Under a superlinear penalty function, registering n clones imposes an attacker cost scaling as O(n^2), rendering identity flooding unprofitable. Node clusters, codenamed juniper, yarrow, and comet, verify unique hardware-rooted proofs; any detected collusion burns the committed collateral, enforcing insurmountable economic friction.
